title: Flat detection of the maximal domain of a relative rational map
statement:
Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning that it has a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $X,X',Y$ be smooth finite-type $S$-schemes [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with $Y$ separated over $S$, meaning that its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Products and fibres are base changes [def-pc-base-change]. An open in an $S$-scheme is $S$-dense when it is dense in every fibre. An $S$-rational map $\phi:X\dashrightarrow Y$ is an equivalence class of $S$-morphisms on $S$-dense opens, two representatives being equivalent when they agree on an $S$-dense common open. The union $\operatorname{dom}(\phi)$ of all representative domains carries a unique morphism representing $\phi$ and restricting to each representative. In particular, two morphisms on $X$ representing the same rational map are equal. If $p:X'\to X$ is a flat $S$-morphism [def-weil-flat-morphism], then $\phi\circ p$ is an $S$-rational map and
$$\operatorname{dom}(\phi\circ p)=p^{-1}\operatorname{dom}(\phi).$$
Consequently, if $p$ is also surjective and $\phi\circ p$ is represented by a morphism on all of $X'$, then $\phi$ is represented by a unique morphism on all of $X$. In particular this applies when $H$ is a smooth finite-type $S$-scheme, $E\subset H\times_SX$ is open, and $p:E\to X$ is the second projection with nonempty fibre over every point of $X$: this projection is flat and surjective, and $E$ is smooth and of finite type over $S$.

proof.text: First note the finiteness needed below. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], $X,X'$ and $Y$ are Noetherian. The product $P=X\times_SY$ is Noetherian as well: its projection to $X$ is finite type by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change], and apply the same Noetherian lemma. Opens in these schemes have quasi-compact inclusions by [lem-sfb-noetherian-open-immersion-qc]. A Noetherian scheme is quasi-separated: on affine charts, intersections of two affine opens are open subsets of a Noetherian affine and hence quasi-compact. Thus a morphism from a quasi-compact one of these opens to a quasi-separated scheme is quasi-compact, by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. In particular all graph maps used below, and restrictions of $p$ between these opens, are quasi-compact. Since $X'\to S$ is locally finite type, cancellation (f) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] makes $p$ locally finite type. Its target is locally Noetherian, so [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth] makes $p$ locally finitely presented.

source.place: BLR 2.5 Proposition 5, finiteness before its first sentence; Stacks 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian), 01TX (lemma-noetherian-finite-type-finite-presentation), 01OX (lemma-immersion-into-noetherian).

proof.text: Two representatives $a:U\to Y$ and $b:V\to Y$ agree on an $S$-dense common open $W\subseteq U\cap V$. The open $U\cap V$ is smooth over $S$ by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes]. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-fibrewise-dense-open-base-change] with the identity base change to see that $W$ is schematically dense there. The relative separated-target uniqueness theorem [lemma-nagata-ext-scheme-theoretically-dominant-separated] therefore gives $a=b$ on $U\cap V$. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing], all representatives glue uniquely on their union $D$. Their structure maps agree over $S$ locally and hence globally by the same gluing uniqueness. The union contains a representative domain, so is $S$-dense, and the glued map represents $\phi$. This also proves the asserted uniqueness for everywhere-defined representatives.

source.place: BLR 2.5, definition on p.55 and graph-domain paragraph on p.57; Stacks 01RH (lemma-equality-of-morphisms).

proof.text: Choose a representative $a:U\to Y$ and let $\Gamma$ be the scheme-theoretic image of $(j_U,a):U\to P$. This means the closed subscheme defined by the kernel of restriction to $U$, by [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-ideal-qc]. The image is independent of representative: if $W\subset U\cap V$ is an $S$-dense common domain, the density lemma gives an injective restriction sheaf map on $U$ and on $V$. On any open of $P$, restriction from its inverse image in $U$ to its inverse image in $W$ is consequently injective. Hence the kernels defining the images of $U$ and $W$ coincide; likewise for $V$ and $W$. This is an equality of defining ideals, so of closed subschemes. Let $q:\Gamma\to X$ be the first projection. By [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-partial-section], $q^{-1}(U)\to U$ is an isomorphism. Independence allows this conclusion for every representative domain.

source.place: BLR 2.5, graph construction p.57; kernel description in Stacks 01R8 (lemma-quasi-compact-scheme-theoretic-image).

proof.text: The domain $D$ is exactly the union of opens $W\subset X$ over which $q$ is an isomorphism. Every representative domain has this property by step 3. Conversely, if $q_W$ is an isomorphism, composing its inverse with the second projection gives a morphism $b:W\to Y$. On $W\cap U$ this equals $a$, since the restriction of $q_W^{-1}$ is the inverse of $q_U$. The maps $a,b$ therefore glue on $U\cup W$ by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. This union is $S$-dense because it contains $U$, so the gluing is a representative of $\phi$ and $W\subset D$. In particular, $q_D$ is an isomorphism: its inverses on representative domains agree, being inverses to the same map, and glue, as do the inverse identities.

For every $s\in S$, the morphism $p_s:X'_s\to X_s$ is flat by [lem-sfb-pointwise-flatness-base-change] and locally finitely presented by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. Thus it is open by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open]. If $O'$ is a nonempty open of $X'_s$, its image is a nonempty open of $X_s$, hence meets the dense open $U_s$. Thus $O'$ meets $p_s^{-1}(U_s)$. This proves $p^{-1}U$ is $S$-dense. Pulling back representatives and their common domains now defines $\phi\circ p$ independently of choices. Step 2, applied to $X'$, constructs its maximal morphism on $D'$. Pulling back the morphism on $D$ proves $p^{-1}D\subset D'$.

source.place: BLR 2.5 Proposition 5, first three sentences; Stacks 01UA (lemma-fppf-open).

proof.text: The morphism $P'=X'\times_SY\to X\times_SY=P$ is a base change of the flat morphism $p$ and hence flat by [lem-sfb-pointwise-flatness-base-change]. Apply [lem-sfb-scheme-image-flat-base-change] to the quasi-compact graph map $U\to P$ of step 3. Its pullback is precisely the graph map $p^{-1}U\to P'$: on a test scheme a point is a pair $(x',u)$ with $p(x')=u$ in $X$, and its $Y$ coordinate is $a(u)$. Therefore the closed graph $\Gamma'$ of $\phi\circ p$ is $\Gamma\times_X X'$ as a closed subscheme of $P'$, compatibly with its first projection $q':\Gamma'\to X'$. This uses the independence of representatives proved in step 3, now for $X'$.

source.place: BLR 2.5 Proposition 5, graph comparison using Proposition 2; Stacks 081I (lemma-flat-base-change-scheme-theoretic-image).

proof.text: Set $V=p(D')$, an open of $X$ by openness of $p$. The map $h:D'\to V$ is surjective by definition and flat as an open restriction of $p$; the latter is the open-base-change case of [lem-sfb-pointwise-flatness-base-change]. It is quasi-compact by step 1: $D'$ is quasi-compact and $V$ quasi-separated. The base change of $q_V:\Gamma\times_XV\to V$ along $h$ is $q'_{D'}$, using the graph comparison in step 6. By step 4 for $X'$, $q'_{D'}$ is an isomorphism. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-isomorphism] with exactly this flat, surjective, quasi-compact $h$ to conclude $q_V$ is an isomorphism. Step 4 gives $V\subset D$. Every $x'\in D'$ has $p(x')\in V\subset D$, so $D'\subset p^{-1}D$. Together with step 5 this proves the domain equality.

If $p$ is surjective and the composite has an everywhere-defined representative, then $D'=X'$ and the proved equality gives $p^{-1}D=X'$. For any $x\in X$, choose $x'$ over $x$; then $x'\in p^{-1}D$ implies $x\in D$. Hence $D=X$, and step 2 supplies the unique morphism on $X$. This also covers empty schemes: a surjection from the empty scheme forces $X$ empty.

Finally put $P_H=H\times_SX$. Its projection $\pi:P_H\to X$ is smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change], applied to $H\to S$, and finite type by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. Composing $\pi$ with the smooth $X\to S$ makes $P_H\to S$ smooth by [lem-trf-smooth-composition]; composition also makes it finite type. Thus $P_H$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. For the open $E\subset P_H$, [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes] makes both $E\to X$ and $E\to S$ smooth, and [sbc-lem-smooth-criterion] makes $E\to X$ flat. Its fibres are nonempty by hypothesis, so it is surjective on points. The open immersion $E\to P_H$ is quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-noetherian-open-immersion-qc] and locally finite type (on affine principal-open charts it is a localization at one element); hence finite type. Composition gives $E\to S$ finite type. The hypotheses already proved for $p$ therefore apply with $X'=E$.

Source: BLR 2.5, read from a local copy of the scan (PDF pp.61-64): S-density on p.55, Lemma 1(b) and Proposition 2 on pp.55-56, the graph as schematic closure and dom = Omega on p.57, Proposition 5 and its proof on p.58. The item matches hypothesis by hypothesis; Noetherian S was already in the seed and replaces BLR Lemma 3. All 19 cited statements say what their steps take. Step 1: 01T6/01T4 make X, X', Y and P Noetherian, opens are qc, qcqs(1) makes the maps quasi-compact, and (f) plus lft->lfp makes p lfp. Step 2: smooth restriction, then the fibrewise-dense lemma with T'=T gives scheme-theoretic density, then the relative separated rigidity (no reducedness needed), then gluing. Step 3: equal kernel ideals give graph independence, then partial-section with a qc open immersion. Step 4: the characterisation of D is elementary. Step 5: p_s is a base change along X_s->X, flat and lfp, hence open, so p^{-1}U is S-dense. Step 6: 081I with g_U qc and U x_P P' = p^{-1}U gives Gamma' = Gamma x_X X'. Step 7: h: D'->V is flat, surjective and qc (D' is qc and V quasi-separated), Gamma x_X D' = q'^{-1}D', then 02L4. Step 8 is elementary. Step 9: smooth base change and composition, finite type, and the open E is qc and lft, so finite type. Edge cases tested: empty schemes and fibres, p non-surjective or the identity, nonreduced S, and the (T+1)/(T-1) example. No cycle. Batch-5 flags are both accepted as generic: lem-trf-smooth-composition is the Mathlib leaf 01VA (sk-i-curve-zero), and the closure of the fibrewise-dense lemma reaches only the generic smoothness nodes lem-trf-smooth-at-point-fibre-criterion (01V9), lem-trf-smooth-fibre-affine-ring-at-prime and lem-trf-affine-smooth-prime-scheme-neighbourhood, none of them part of the trace formula or Poincare duality. lean.statement: theorem relative_rational_flat_regularity {S X X' Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian S] (sX : X ⟶ S) (sX' : X' ⟶ S) (sY : Y ⟶ S) [Smooth sX] [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] [QuasiCompact sX] [Smooth sX'] [LocallyOfFiniteType sX'] [QuasiCompact sX'] [Smooth sY] [LocallyOfFiniteType sY] [QuasiCompact sY] [IsSeparated sY] : (∀ φ : Scheme.RelativeRationalMap sX sY, (∃! f : φ.domain.toScheme ⟶ Y, φ.Represents φ.domain f ∧ ∀ (a : Scheme.RelativePartialMap sX sY), a.classOf = φ → ∀ h : a.domain ≤ φ.domain, X.homOfLE h ≫ f = a.hom) ∧ (∀ f g : X ⟶ Y, φ.Represents ⊤ (X.topIso.hom ≫ f) → φ.Represents ⊤ (X.topIso.hom ≫ g) → f = g) ∧ (∀ (p : X' ⟶ X), p ≫ sX = sX' → Flat p → ∃! ψ : Scheme.RelativeRationalMap sX' sY, φ.IsComposite p ψ ∧ ψ.domain = p ⁻¹ᵁ φ.domain ∧ (Surjective p → (∃ f : X' ⟶ Y, ψ.Represents ⊤ (X'.topIso.hom ≫ f)) → ∃! f : X ⟶ Y, φ.Represents ⊤ (X.topIso.hom ≫ f)))) ∧ (∀ (H : Scheme.{u}) (sH : H ⟶ S), Smooth sH → LocallyOfFiniteType sH → QuasiCompact sH → ∀ E : (pullback sH sX).Opens, (∀ x : X, Nonempty ((E.ι ≫ pullback.snd sH sX).fiber x)) → Flat (E.ι ≫ pullback.snd sH sX) ∧ Surjective (E.ι ≫ pullback.snd sH sX) ∧ Smooth (E.ι ≫ pullback.snd sH sX ≫ sX) ∧ LocallyOfFiniteType (E.ι ≫ pullback.snd sH sX ≫ sX) ∧ QuasiCompact (E.ι ≫ pullback.snd sH sX ≫ sX))
